text: The full gate contains a one-second wall-time assertion that can fail when isolated agent worktrees compile concurrently; serialize repository-wide validation or replace wall-clock pass/fail with a contention-tolerant contract.

The historical support-collapse note still describes a PNG-only RealFixture loader, while current code accepts PNG and JPEG. Reusing that prose as current task context falsely blocks existing corpora; verify the loader source and label old replay limitations as historical.

just check core phase is red on unchanged main (dd61cc4) under Swift 6.4 / macOS 27.0: 14 tests across ImageRendererGoldenTests, SnapshotTests, BuiltInPaletteSnapshotTests, MaskSnapshotTests, CompositionSnapshotTests and EffectKernelSnapshotTests fail byte/pixel golden comparison (64 issues). Reproduced on main with a filtered run, so it is toolchain/OS rendering drift, not branch changes. Fail-fast ordering then skips media, sentinel and DocC phases; run them separately until goldens are re-baselined with a no-harm census or the toolchain is pinned.

A shell cancellation test signalled the whole process group and missed parent-only SIGTERM: Bash deferred its foreground-command trap, leaving a regenerated artifact and lock until the child exited. Test supervisor-style cancellation and wait for every regeneration writer to stop before restoring the artifact.

Swift Testing on Swift 6.4 rejects a #require nested inside another #require's argument (recursive macro expansion), so the whole test target fails to build; Linux Swift 6.2 syntax-parsing did not catch it. Hoist the inner value into its own let.

Agent-authored PRs verified only on Linux (no xcrun) reached the native gate with a test-target compile error and a CommandSurfaceTests expectation broken by a justfile recipe change; run just check-fast natively before calling a Swift change verified.

BuildResearchIndex treats --help and unknown arguments as regeneration, so a capability probe rewrites the generated research index. Use the documented --check mode for read-only validation; explicit argument parsing would prevent the surprise.

BuildStandardVectors --audit writes the fixed date 2026-09-04 into every result.yaml, including later audits. Record the actual capture date before retaining a new audit; deriving the manifest date from the run would preserve provenance.

Exact-render PNG goldens can differ by one 8-bit step between two Macs with identical macOS, Xcode and Swift builds; a re-baseline verified on one host broke the gate on another. Verify a golden re-record on a second host (or the original recording host) before treating it as an OS-version baseline.

The README hero PNG was committed with no recorded command, build, or post-processing, so a later 'regression' claimed against it cost a 19-build bisect before showing the image itself was never a plain Aski render. Record the exact command and build next to any showcase image, and keep its caption true to that command.

Deleting a merged PR's head branch closed a draft PR stacked on it (GitHub closes, does not retarget, a PR whose base branch is deleted). Recovery: re-push the base ref, gh pr reopen, gh pr edit --base main. Prevent: run gh pr list --base <branch> before deleting any merged branch.

SwiftPM builds in a fresh git worktree fail Git's safe.bareRepository check; exporting GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'safe.bareRepository=all'" for the build process fixes it without touching global config, but the workaround is recorded only in one research note, so each new worktree worker rediscovers it. Document it in CONTRIBUTING.md's worktree setup.

CGColor(red:green:blue:alpha:) creates a Generic RGB color (gamma about 1.8), while CIColor(red:green:blue:alpha:) creates an sRGB color. Rebuilding a CIColor from a CGColor's raw components therefore silently reinterprets the color; keep the original CGColor (copy(alpha:) to change alpha) or convert it explicitly. Fixtures built with CGColor(red:) can hide the bug.

An MP4 with no color tags leaves the Y'CbCr matrix to the decoder: AVAssetReader chose BT.601 for frames narrower than about 768 px and BT.709 above, shifting saturated colors. Tag the track with AVVideoColorPropertiesKey plus matching CVBuffer attachments, and check the written VUI with: ffmpeg -i out.mp4 -c copy -bsf:v trace_headers -f null -

In an async context such as an async Swift Testing test, ASCIIGrid.renderImage(font:backgroundColor:scale:) resolves to the async throwing effects overload instead of the synchronous plain renderer, so a parity test written for the plain path failed to compile (PR 12 groundwork). Passing an argument only the plain overload has, such as preserveSourceAspect:, selects it; overload names that differ by path would remove the trap.

swift package diagnose-api-breaking-changes v0.7.0 cannot build the release baseline: under Swift Build the package-benchmark plugin input is missing, and with --build-system native it fails on module redefinitions, then 'Failed to load module: Aski'. The v0.8.0 API-break inventory fell back to a diff scan of public/open declarations and enum cases in Sources/Aski. A baseline-buildable recipe (or a scripted public-declaration diff) would make release notes' source-break claims tool-checked.

evidence.cmd: xcrun swift package diagnose-api-breaking-changes v0.7.0 --products Aski
